title: Your Grocery Store App Is Spying on You
editorialNotes: Slide 7 carries "No ads. No data selling." verbatim; this is a product-behaviour claim about a pre-launch app, flag for Adi if it is not yet true.
Tracking claims sourced to FTC retail data-collection reports in the Notion source index.

copy.headline: Your grocery store's "rewards" app is a surveillance tool.
Purchase frequency.
items: The app knows how often you buy milk, eggs, bread — down to the day.
When you're "late," it sends a push notification with a coupon. That's not generosity. That's a trigger to get you back in the store.

copy.headline: Brand switching.
copy.body: If you buy Store Brand once after buying Name Brand for months, the app flags it. Expect a Name Brand coupon within 48 hours. The brand paid for that coupon through a trade promotion budget.

copy.headline: Cart composition.
items: The app cross-references what you buy together.
If you always buy pasta + sauce + cheese, it starts recommending wine or garlic bread.
It's upselling based on your own patterns.

copy.headline: Price sensitivity score.
copy.body: Some loyalty programs assign you an internal price tier. Frequent coupon users get more coupons. Full-price buyers see fewer discounts. You might be paying more than the person next to you for the same item.

copy.headline: Location data.
items: Some apps track which aisles you walk through and how long you linger.
This data gets sold to brands who then pay for shelf placement in the zones you visit most.

copy.headline: Your loyalty app rewards you with convenience. It rewards the store with your entire behavioral profile.
copy.ctaLine: fond tracks your kitchen — not your behavior. No ads. No data selling. Link in bio.
